newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close lower on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close lower on political worries.

text.p: Indian shares finished lower in nervous trade on Monday as investors stayed on the sidelines after former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao quit as Congress party chief over the weekend, dealers said.
They said prices would stay shaky as the Congress began its search for a new leader. The Congress Working Committee is due to meet later in the day to elect a provisional new leader.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index ended 15.69 points, or 0.47 percent lower at 3,331.09 after dropping to an intra-day low of 3,307.20.
Rao's abrupt decision on Saturday to quit the presidency of India's oldest party came after a New Delhi court ordered him to appear as a co-accused in a cheating case.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 8.91 points to end at 968.84 while the 500-share CRISIL index dropped 4.88 points to 651.63.
Traders said the news would worry the market but would not be construed as overly negative.
"There is no uncertainty for the existing government," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage. "If anything, it might make them stronger."
The Congress party's support is crucial for the survival of the 13-party minority coalition government led by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
SBI lost 2.0 rupees to 261.25, TISCO 2.50 to 171.75 and Reliance 1.25 to 195, Bajaj Auto 13.75 to 975.25, ACC 10.50 to 1,851.25 and ITC 1.0 to 294.
The Delhi index lost 6.14 points to 736.51, the Calcutta index 3.24 to 428.83 and the Madras index 20.99 points to 3,416.80.
